strengths: Well-motivated practical problem: addresses expensive re-alignment costs when adapting MLLMs to newer LLMs
Comprehensive empirical evaluation on 7 benchmarks with consistent improvements; extensive ablations and case studies
Clever CRO reward design using downstream reasoning success to close perception-reasoning loop
Compelling scalability results (Figure 1) showing better performance-to-parameter tradeoffs; plug-and-play adaptation across reasoner sizes is practically valuable
Thorough documentation with prompts, hyperparameters, training dynamics supporting reproducibility; human evaluation confirms automated metrics
Demonstrates consistent gains across model sizes (3B-32B) and multiple reasoning domains (math, science, logic)
weaknesses: Limited core novelty: perceptual decoupling is concurrent work; applying GRPO to captions is straightforward adaptation, not fundamental innovation
Confounded experimental design: RACRO models trained on ViRL39K (38,870 samples) with unclear if baselines receive equivalent RL training; comparison with InternVL3-78B-MPO not apples-to-apples

Critical unresolved inconsistency (Table 3): Cap. alone outperforms Cap.+Sol. during training, yet inference uses both, suggesting reasoner may ignore captions and use Sol. as shortcut during inference—undermines perceptual decoupling narrative
Insufficient transfer analysis: claims optimal captions transfer across reasoners but no systematic study of how CRO-optimized captions for R1-7B perform with Qwen3-8B or R1-32B
Missing computational cost analysis: inference requires running reasoner for every sample; training requires reward calls—expensive overhead not quantified; no wall-clock time comparisons
Reward signal limitations: binary exact-match (Eq. 2) is brittle; parse() function not formally specified; unknown applicability to open-ended reasoning with multiple valid answers
Statistical rigor absent: no error bars, confidence intervals, or multiple runs; some differences <1% without significance testing; single-run results
Incomplete failure analysis: no systematic study of failure modes, which task types benefit most, or when decoupling hurts performance; Appendix D shows cherry-picked successes only

strengths: Addresses a practically important problem: enabling advanced reasoning LLMs in multimodal settings without expensive re-alignment
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across seven diverse benchmarks with detailed ablations and human evaluation
Demonstrates strong empirical results and achieved state-of-the-art average performance on tested benchmarks
Practical value of plug-and-play adaptation to new reasoning LLMs without retraining
Informative case studies with visual examples and clear presentation of the overall framework
weaknesses: Limited novelty: perceptual decoupling and GRPO-based caption optimization are not novel; the contribution is primarily engineering existing techniques

Weak mechanistic understanding: paper fails to explain why binary reward signals should improve caption quality specifically, and training-inference mismatch (captions only during training vs. with tentative solutions at inference) is underexplored

Experimental design concerns: confounding variables in Table 1 (different sizes/reasoners/CRO applied simultaneously), no statistical significance testing, no error bars or multiple runs reported, several unexplained negative results (e.g., -1.4% on MathVista)

Scalability claims need qualification: Figure 1 averages heterogeneous benchmarks and compares different model sizes with different reasoners; generalization shown only empirically for limited LLM variants
Narrow evaluation scope: tested only on math/science reasoning tasks; generalization to other multimodal tasks (VQA, visual understanding) is unexplored and acknowledged as limitation
Missing ablations and analysis: no sensitivity to hyperparameters, no reward design justification, no analysis of when/why CRO fails, no comparison with alternative RL approaches

Inconsistent results not explained: performance varies dramatically across benchmarks (MathVision +14.4% vs. MathVista +0.0%), some benchmarks show degradation, the finding that tentative solutions hurt caption-based rewards is not analyzed

strengths: Clear motivation addressing a practical bottleneck: computational cost of re-aligning vision-language models when upgrading reasoning LLMs
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: 7 benchmarks, multiple baseline categories, 3 model sizes, detailed ablations, and human evaluation validating automated results
Well-demonstrated practical scalability: plug-and-play adaptation to stronger reasoner LLMs (Qwen3-8B, R1-32B) without retraining, with validation in Figure 5
Evidence of caption quality improvement beyond metrics: pairwise comparisons with GPT-4o, human evaluation (85% consistency), and detailed case studies showing before/after improvements
Consistent state-of-the-art performance across diverse tasks: MathVista, MathVision, MathVerse, MMMU, WeMath, DynaMath, LogicVista with gains of 3-6% on average
Rigorous supplementary materials: extensive case studies (Tables 7-18), prompt templates, training dynamics visualization supporting reproducibility
Complementary analysis showing CRO and GRPO address different aspects, with combined improvements demonstrating orthogonal contributions
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: CRO is essentially GRPO applied to caption generation; perceptual decoupling itself is acknowledged as non-novel and similar to concurrent work

Missing computational cost analysis: no breakdown of training costs for CRO (requires 4× reasoner forward passes per example) or inference costs compared to end-to-end models—critical for evaluating practical value

Modest empirical improvements lacking statistical significance: many gains are 1-5% without confidence intervals or significance tests; improvements over large baselines (e.g., 54.6% vs 54.6%) are marginal

Incomplete analysis of when/why the approach works: limited investigation of why captions with reasoning rewards improve reasoning, why captions alone perform poorly (Table 2), or failure modes where decoupling is suboptimal

Fundamental tension unexplained: captions alone underperform tentative solutions on many tasks (Table 2), yet the approach claims captions capture sufficient visual information—this gap in reasoning is not well addressed

Limited scope and generalization: evaluated exclusively on math/science/logic tasks; applicability to other vision domains (medical imaging, scene understanding) and fine-grained spatial reasoning unclear
Incomplete ablations: no sensitivity analysis for key hyperparameters (# rollouts, clipping ε, KL penalty β); hyperparameter choices appear arbitrary and unjustified
Experimental setup concerns: modest training data (38K examples), arbitrary choice of R1-7B as training reasoner, limited analysis of sensitivity to these choices
Missing implementation clarity: verl framework poorly described; hyperparameter justification absent; notation distinctions (Pcap vs Pcot) could be clearer upfront

strengths: Addresses practical and timely problem of leveraging advancing reasoning LLMs without expensive retraining
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 7 benchmarks with extensive baselines, ablations, and model sizes
Strong empirical results (+11.2% for 7B, 58% average with GPT-OSS-120B) with superior performance-efficiency trade-offs
Thoughtful algorithm design with clever caption penalty to prevent reward hacking and VPO reward based on downstream task correctness
Demonstrates effective generalization to unseen LLMs (Section 4.3), enabling true plug-and-play scaling
Thorough documentation with prompt templates, training dynamics analysis, human evaluation, and case studies
Both GPT-4 and human evaluation confirm improved caption quality with VPO (87% human-GPT agreement)
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: caption-then-reason pipelines are established; VPO is essentially GRPO applied to captions; main contribution is incremental combination
Critical training-inference objective mismatch: VPO trained on qcap-only (Eq. 2) but inference uses qcap+sol (Fig. 12); Footnote 5 acknowledges but doesn't resolve
Reward hacking prevention mechanism is fragile: relies on LLM-based hasCap() check via few-shot prompting with no analysis of false positives/negatives
Training uses R1-7B as reward LLM but inference with Qwen3-8B—Table 3 shows R1-7B significantly outperforms, indicating distribution shift and potential misalignment
Domain-specific evaluation: optimized exclusively for math/science reasoning; general benchmarks (Fig. 5) don't test full reasoning pipelines; applicability to other domains unclear
Limited caption-then-reason baseline comparisons: only ECSO and OmniCaptioner; many recent distillation methods missing
Incomplete technical justification: why sequential VPO→GRPO vs. joint? Why binary reward vs. nuanced scoring? Small-scale human evaluation (100 samples)
Computational efficiency analysis incomplete: absolute training cost still substantial (550M tokens); inference cost of external LLM not compared to monolithic MLLM
Missing systematic analysis: no characterization of question types benefiting from VPO, non-monotonic improvements with LLM size (Fig. 10) suggests potential brittleness

strengths: Addresses a practical and timely problem: upgrading MLLMs to use state-of-the-art reasoning models without expensive retraining
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 7 benchmarks with extensive baselines, ablations, and supplementary analysis
Strong empirical results with favorable accuracy-to-model-size trade-offs
Enables a practical inference-time scaling paradigm—pairing optimized MLLMs with any external LLM
Thorough implementation details and reproducibility efforts with case studies and qualitative analysis
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: perception-reasoning decoupling builds on existing caption-then-reason pipelines; VPO is essentially GRPO with a modified reward function

Questionable design choices inadequately justified: (1) Training uses P'_reason (without tentative solution) while inference uses P_reason (with it); (2) Default is qcap+sol despite Table 3 showing qcap-only performs better during VPO training
Reward hacking and ad-hoc fix: The caption penalty (Eq. 3) using LLM-based hasCap() checking suggests fundamental reward signal design is flawed; robustness unclear

Overstated 'LLM-agnostic' claims: Figure 9 shows caption length depends on training LLM; Table 3 shows R1-7B is optimal for training; different LLMs yield different characteristics—VPO is LLM-dependent, not LLM-agnostic
Missing critical comparisons: No ablation showing VPO contribution vs. simply pairing original MLLM with stronger LLM (Qwen3-8B); unclear if improvements come from VPO or just better external LLM

Narrow scope and limited generalization: Explicitly designed for math/science reasoning with slow-thinking LLMs; general benchmarks don't test full reasoning pipeline; no evidence on other multi-modal reasoning tasks
Lack of mechanistic insight: Paper shows empirically that captions improve but provides no understanding of why outcome-based rewards lead to better captions or what VPO actually optimizes for

Incomplete computational analysis: No inference latency analysis despite sequential MLLM→LLM pipeline; training FLOP comparison vs. end-to-end methods is not apples-to-apples; practical deployment costs unclear

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 7 benchmarks with extensive baselines and ablations; results are consistently strong and well-documented
Addresses a practical problem (expensive MLLM retraining) with an elegant decoupling solution; inference-time scaling without retraining is a novel capability
Thorough supporting materials including human evaluation (87% GPT-human consistency), detailed case studies, and training dynamics analysis demonstrating caption quality improvements
Strong empirical results with superior performance-size trade-offs; 15B model outperforms 72B+ baselines; best average accuracy of 58% across benchmarks
Sound technical approach combining GRPO with reasoning-aligned reward signal; effective sequential training strategy with clear ablation showing each component's contribution
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: caption-then-reason pipelines are established; VPO is primarily GRPO applied to captioning; main contribution is engineering/combination rather than fundamental innovation

Ad-hoc caption penalty mechanism (Eq. 3) required to prevent reward hacking suggests structural issues with base VPO formulation; detecting captions via few-shot prompting is inelegant and lacks theoretical justification
Training-inference asymmetry (qcap only during training vs qcap+sol at inference) justified only by empirical findings; lacks principled explanation and appears to be an optimization trick

Scope explicitly limited to math/science reasoning; general benchmarks show comparable (not improved) performance; extension to other domains unclear; generalization to stronger training LLMs shows degradation

Insufficient analysis of what VPO learns: beyond showing captions are longer/more detailed, lacks systematic analysis of specific information VPO encourages or comparison to supervised caption optimization approaches
